comments.text:
As someone in the AI hardware and model architecture research space, I don't think this should have any impact on Nvidia. So what if it's more efficient to train? Many of those algorithmic improvements work on the current Nvidia GPUs (even the V100s, but much less efficiently - still better than nothing). Nvidia is already moving towards native low-bit quantization support and improving their interconnects, so this wouldn't affect their current strategy. And all this says is the big US AI companies need to be a bit smarter about how they train their models (no surprise to academic researchers who do good research on the comparison of a shoe-string budget - maybe 4 - 16 A100s for a couple of months). Meanwhile, a lot can be learned from the DeepSeek papers (not just the R1 paper), which again can be applied to the existing infrastructure. 
So really, the only rationale way this will affect stocks is if we assume that R1-Zero /is/ ASI and we just solved AI with no new research needed, which frankly is absurd. Otherwise, you're betting against labs who may be working on different (equally important) problems (e.g. long context inference and active memories - Titans?).
